title: The Heritage Hopper
subtitle: CrossFit Maker Challenge, 2nd Place
pitch: A working SLS-printed miniature of the 2007 hopper that picked the first CrossFit Games workouts, designed, manufactured, and delivered for a Design-Make-Sell competition sponsored by CrossFit LLC.
highlights: Selected in the top 3 of 17 entries into the production phase
Field research at 15 CrossFit gyms across the South Bay
Designed the full CAD in SolidWorks, including the spinning hopper and a concealed push-push coin mechanism
Team selected to potentially mass-produce the item; a bulk quote was submitted for up to 450 units

blocks.md: The CrossFit Maker Challenge is the SCU Maker Lab's Design-Make-Sell competition, sponsored by CrossFit LLC, for a CrossFit Games 20th-anniversary commemorative product. Our product, The Heritage Hopper, is a working miniature of the 2007 "Peanut Roaster" hopper: the drum spins, the door opens, and it sits on a laser-engraved cherry base with a hidden push-push challenge-coin display mechanism. I was the Project Lead and coordinated directly with CrossFit's point of contact through a shipped QC unit, feedback rounds, and final delivery.

blocks.heading: From research to delivery
items: Visited 15 CrossFit gyms across the South Bay and interviewed gymgoers in person.
Designed the full product CAD in SolidWorks, including the spinning hopper mechanism and the concealed coin mechanism (springs, pivot pins, latch).
Ran the material journey: an iron-filled HTPLA prototype, then matte PETG, then production SLS nylon with a rust-effect finish and thicker walls after the sponsor's drop-test feedback.
Manufactured the run: SLS and FDM prints, sand-blasting, wood finishing, laser engraving, CNC machining of the first-unit base, coin-mechanism assembly, packaging, and QC.
